questions.question: In CMI Problem 1 ($2023 \times 2023$ real symmetric matrix $A$ with $|a_{ij} - 2023| \le 1$), what are the minimum and maximum possible values of its largest eigenvalue $\lambda(A)$?
questions.explanation: Testing unit vector $\mathbf{1}$ gives $\lambda(A) \ge \langle A\mathbf{1}, \mathbf{1}\rangle \ge 2022\cdot 2023$, while Cauchy–Schwarz bounds $\|Av\| \le 2024\cdot 2023 \|v\|$; matrices $2022J$ and $2024J$ attain both.

questions.question: In CMI Problem 4 ($\chi(G) = k$ with red/blue edge coloring), what theorem extracts a $k$-element independent-set coloring layer if all monochromatic components have size $\le k - 1$?
questions.explanation: Any $j$ red blocks of size $\ell = k-1$ have $j\ell$ vertices and must touch at least $j$ blue blocks of size $\ell$, so Hall's condition gives a perfect matching of size $m$ whose representatives form a valid color class.

questions.question: In CMI Problem 5, why does $(1 + 1/p_N)^N \to 1$ as $N \to \infty$?

options.text: Because $p_N / N \sim \ln N \to \infty$, so $(1 + 1/p_N)^N \le e^{N/p_N} \to e^0 = 1$

questions.explanation: By the Prime Number Theorem ($\S 9$), $p_N \sim N \ln N$, so $N / p_N \to 0$ and $e^{N/p_N} \to 1$.

questions.question: In CMI Problem 3, why does bounding $f(x, y) \le g(x) + g(y)$ always succeed on $\mathbb{Q} \times \mathbb{Q}$ yet fail for some $f$ on $\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}$?

options.text: $\mathbb{Q}$ can be enumerated sequentially so each new element dominates all finite prefixes, whereas $|\mathbb{R}| = |\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}|$ allows diagonalizing against every $g$

questions.explanation: Countability of $\mathbb{Q}$ lets us take finite prefix maxima $S_i \times S_i$, whereas indexing sequences $\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$ by $\mathbb{R}$ defeats every candidate $g$ via diagonalization.
